storyResolution.notes: Each tag resolves to exactly one doc (no ambiguity). All five are auto-complete, i.e. approved by machine with no human review. Every first-party file under src/, script/ and test/ was added by a [story-NNN] commit.

conformanceSummary.story-001: CONFORMS. Constructor rejects zero addresses. setRoute checks token!=0, path[0]==token and that the last non-zero path entry equals the live rewardToken. clearRoute, getRoute, setEthPool (currency0 native, currency1 rewardToken) and getEthPool all present. Toolchain is 0.8.26/cancun/optimizer on/via_ir off, and the remappings are identical in both files. The 'no harvest function' criterion is point-in-time and story-002 superseded it, so test_noHarvestFunction is vacuous (CODE-007(1))
conformanceSummary.story-002: CONFORMS to Flow steps 1-8: access check, live rewardToken, borrow calc*1.01, approve/claim/reset, sell loop with zero-token, reward and zero-balance skips, RouteNotConfigured, settle by actual delta (disclosed Decision 4), EthPoolNotSet, receive gated to the PoolManager. Two Law-1 notes on the story's own prescriptions: F-02 and F-03. Background premise is wrong: F-04
conformanceSummary.story-003: CONFORMS. g0=gasleft() is the first statement (L230). The pull is conditional on nftIndex!=0 && nftMinter!=0. The whole-balance refund runs after the unlock and before payout. Unprofitable formula matches the doc. Required NatSpec is present
conformanceSummary.story-004: CONFORMS. Fork suite pinned at 26261000 and skips loudly when no RPC is set. Every address verified, routes asserted on chain, deepest-pool assertion, end-to-end harvest asserts NFT burn and zero balances (ETH/USDC/DOLA/USDe/crvUSD/FRAX/strategy tokens/NFT). Explicit no-nested-unlock test, each-strategy-exempt loop, Unprofitable and InsufficientEthOut tests, GAS_OVERHEAD=60k with calibration comment and assertion. The double-fee comment copies the story's wrong mechanism (ECON-002)
conformanceSummary.story-005: CONFORMS on every Technical-Details step: fees 2*base+tip, fee-carrying estimate and call (order swapped, disclosed in Decision 3, at least as strict), bc integer wei, minEthOut formula with abort, keystore-only signing with raw-key refusal, PRIVATE_RPC_URL defaulting to Flashbots with chain-id cross-check, DRY_RUN, summary printed before send, no secrets echoed. Anvil test proves the success path and abort-before-send with the nonce unchanged. One acceptance gap: F-05

findings.subtype: spec-conflict (design-doc purpose vs settled design decision and stories)
findings.severity: potential-low (carried by ECON-001; do not double-count)
findings.specText: src/CLAUDE.md Purpose: "A claim therefore has positive expected value whenever `market value of the yield tokens - discounted USDC payment > gas + NFT cost`."  versus  src/CLAUDE.md settled 'Gas check' bullet, story-003 Acceptance "The gas check reverts `Unprofitable` when `ethOut < (gasUsedSoFar + GAS_OVERHEAD) * tx.gasprice`" and story-005 Overview "Derives a `minEthOut` that guarantees the gas is covered."
findings.specSource: src/CLAUDE.md (Purpose + Design decisions); story-003 doc Acceptance; story-005 doc Story Overview step 4 / Technical Details step 4
findings.actualBehavior: Both gates price only gas. The on-chain check is (g0-gasleft+60k)*tx.gasprice. The script floor is gasLimit*maxFee+MIN_PROFIT_WEI, with MIN_PROFIT_WEI defaulting to 0. Neither prices the claim-NFT unit that SYA burns. Story-005's own Anvil 'profitable' case reports success after burning NFT index 1 (mint price ~10.78 USDC) for a net of ~0.00365 ETH (~8.5 USD).
findings.deviation: The code faithfully implements stories 003 and 005, and the stories faithfully implement the settled Gas-check decision. Only the CLAUDE.md Purpose invariant ('> gas + NFT cost') fails to hold. The project spec contradicts itself: the purpose names NFT cost, while every lower-level spec (design decision, story-003, story-005, README) names only gas. This is a spec-level gap, not an implementation slip.
findings.law1Assessment: Not story-unsafe under Law 1. The loss is the operator's own (at most one NFT per tx), no third party extracts value and the protocol is not harmed. Severity stays with ECON-001.
findings.recommendation: Owner to reconcile the spec. Either amend story-005, or add a follow-up story, so the floor includes NFTMinterV2.getPrice(nftIndex) converted to ETH (or so MIN_PROFIT_WEI must be set at least that high), or reword the CLAUDE.md Purpose. Until then the README should state that MIN_PROFIT_WEI must cover the NFT's value.

findings.subtype: faithful implementation of an insufficient story rule; footgun (Law 3 in scope)
findings.storyTag: story-001 (rule) -> breaks story-002 acceptance and src/CLAUDE.md invariants
findings.severity: potential-low (carried by CODE-001; do not double-count)
findings.specText: story-001 Technical Details: "`setRoute` validates `path[0] == token` ... It also checks that the last non-zero entry of `path` equals `sya.rewardToken()` ... Use the CurveAMMAdapter loop as the template."  versus  src/CLAUDE.md: "Route coverage invariant ... otherwise the harvest reverts rather than stranding tokens in the contract" / "The contract holds no balances between calls" and story-002 Acceptance: "After a successful harvest the contract holds zero balances of every token."
findings.specSource: story-001 doc (Technical Details > Contract surface); story-002 doc Acceptance; src/CLAUDE.md Design decisions
findings.actualBehavior: setRoute implements story-001's last-non-zero rule exactly. Router NG stops at the first zero pool slot, so a path with an interior gap passes validation, delivers the intermediate token (crvUSD in the CODE-001 fork run) and strands it permanently. The harvest still succeeds and harvest.sh sends it.
findings.deviation: Faithful to story-001, but story-001's rule cannot uphold the invariants that story-002 and CLAUDE.md promise. The story's validation is the root cause, so a fix has to amend the story's rule as well as the code. MockCurveRouter copies the same rule (CODE-007(2)), which hides the problem in the unit tests.
findings.law1Assessment: Law 1 overrides Law 2: the faithful implementation is still a defect. The owner registering a gapped route is a non-obvious owner footgun, because the validator is presented as the route-end guard. Impact: silent, recurring stranding of the caller's paid-for yield. No third-party theft.
findings.recommendation: As in CODE-001: require contiguity (the first empty pool slot k gives path[2k]==rewardToken, with everything after it zero). Also add an end-of-callback zero-balance assertion and make MockCurveRouter follow Router NG semantics.

findings.subtype: story-prescribed balance-based coverage check conflicts with the stateless invariant
findings.severity: potential-low (carried by CODE-002; do not double-count)
findings.specText: story-002 Flow step 5: "Skip if `IERC20(token).balanceOf(this) == 0`. Otherwise, if `!routes[token].configured`, revert `RouteNotConfigured(token)`."  versus  src/CLAUDE.md: "Public, stateless between calls ... The contract holds no balances between calls."
findings.specSource: story-002 doc Technical Details > Flow; src/CLAUDE.md Design decisions
findings.actualBehavior: The implementation follows the story: it acts on the raw balanceOf, not on what SYA delivered in this call. A 1-wei donation of a non-delivering strategy's token makes every harvest revert, either through RouteNotConfigured or through a Router NG dust revert.
findings.deviation: Faithful to story-002. The story's balance-based rule assumes the 'holds no balances' invariant, which any outsider can break by donating tokens, so the story's own mechanism enables the DoS.
findings.law1Assessment: Story-level root of a liveness griefing vector (no fund loss). The fix has to change the story's rule, for example selling only the claim's balance delta or applying a dust threshold.

findings.subtype: story premise factually wrong; implementation and NatSpec inherit it
findings.specText: story-002 Background: "`calculateClaimAmount` (lines 777-814) applies the same skips and sums `totalBalanceOf − principalOf` ... On live strategies it **over-estimates by about 10%** ... This is the safe direction"; Concern [Borrow over-estimate]: "...on top of `BORROW_BUFFER_BPS = 100`. This is the safe direction ... No change needed."
findings.actualBehavior: Live SYA calculateClaimAmount (../stable-yield-accumulator/src/src/StableYieldAccumulator.sol:807-813) returns the discounted, denormalised payment, not gross surplus. Its over-estimate is strategy-dependent: CODE-005 measured paid/estimate as USDC 99.00%, USDe 75.12%, DOLA 100.00%. For DOLA the 1% BORROW_BUFFER_BPS is the only headroom. The harvester NatSpec (L266-267) repeats the false '~10%' claim. The story-002 reviewer noticed the 'gross' mismatch but filed it as a mock observation only.
findings.deviation: The code meets the story's behavioural criterion (borrow = calc*1.01, with the excess settled back). The story's safety reasoning is false for at least one live strategy, so the 'safe direction' assurance does not hold as written. A strategy that delivers more than estimate*1.01 would revert the claim on SYA's allowance pull. That is a loud DoS, not a loss.
findings.law1Assessment: No exploit. The failure is fail-loud only.
findings.recommendation: Correct the story-002 premise and the NatSpec. Optionally size BORROW_BUFFER_BPS from measured worst-case delivery/estimate, and add a MockSYA mode in which delivery exceeds the estimate.

findings.specText: story-005 Acceptance: "It aborts with a readable reason on any simulated revert or an unprofitable estimate." (Technical Details step 2: "On revert, abort and print the decoded reason (`cast call` prints it; map the custom errors `Unprofitable`, `InsufficientEthOut` and `RouteNotConfigured` by name...)")
findings.specSource: story-005 doc Acceptance + Technical Details step 2
findings.actualBehavior: KNOWN_ERRORS lists only SYAHarvester's 10 custom errors. Errors raised inside SYA.claim and the strategies are not decoded. Examples are ZeroAmount() 0x1f2a2005 (the normal 'nothing to claim' outcome), NoValidNFT() 0x0d78b379 (operator lacks the NFT), ExemptStrategyNotRegistered, Pausable EnforcedPause, Tokemak InvalidDataReturned() 0x8d54ba1f (the stale-oracle mode that story-004 flagged for 005) and Router NG empty-data dust reverts. These fall through to the raw passthrough. Verified locally with cast 1.5.1 and anvil: a ZeroAmount revert in a fee-carrying `cast call`/`cast estimate` prints `execution reverted: * , data: "0x1f2a2005"`, and decode_revert passes that through unchanged.
findings.deviation: The script meets the narrower step-2 mandate (it decodes the three named errors and seven more) but not the acceptance wording 'readable reason on any simulated revert'. For the commonest abort causes the operator sees only a bare 4-byte selector and cannot tell which strategy to exempt. Abort-before-send still holds, so safety is unaffected.
findings.law1Assessment: No exploit. The script still aborts before sending.
findings.recommendation: Add SYA's and the known strategy and oracle error signatures to KNOWN_ERRORS (or fall back to `cast decode-error` / the openchain signature lookup). For InvalidDataReturned, print an 'exempt the USDC strategy' hint, as story-004's review requested.

crossReferencesNoNewFinding.note: The wrong 'moves its price against the second trade' mechanism comes from story-004's own text (Background > Routes 'Profitability note' and Concern [Double fee]). test/fork/SYAHarvester.fork.t.sol and MainnetRoutes.sol copy it faithfully. The fix belongs in the story text and the comments, and there is no code deviation.

test_noHarvestFunction encoded story-001's point-in-time acceptance 'no harvest function'. Story-002 superseded that criterion and disclosed the stale test (Decision 7), but no story removed it. It is vacuous, not a deviation.

Story-001's Implementation Notes accepted the set-time rewardToken check: 'harmless, because the harvest-time coverage check (002) and the settle step would fail loudly'. CODE-004 shows the owner cannot pre-stage the new configuration either, so the accepted risk is wider than the story assumed. Severity stays with CODE-004.

Story-002 Decision 4 claimed that settling the actual delta 'would still net every currency to zero' if the price limit cut the swap short. That is true for the PoolManager, but the unswapped reward token then stays in the harvester, against story-002's acceptance 'zero balances of every token'. Unreachable at harvest sizes, so it is already covered as info by CODE-006.

verifiedConformant: src/CLAUDE.md 'Nested unlock hazard': no route step touches V4. The fork test test_fork_harvest_usdeStrategyNonExempt_noNestedUnlock and the full three-strategy harvest prove that the live USDC, USDe and DOLA strategies do not nest an unlock.
src/CLAUDE.md 'One slippage check': routes run with _expected=0 and SYA minRewardTokenSupplied=0. minEthOut is the only bound.
src/CLAUDE.md 'Reward-token skip': rewardToken is read live at L280 and never hard-coded.

story-005 'minEthOut guarantees gas is covered': the floor gasLimit*maxFeePerGas is at least gasUsed*effectiveGasPrice for any includable tx, and it also dominates the on-chain Unprofitable check. This holds except for the NFT cost (F-01).
story-005 key handling: no raw-key path exists, the password is never printed and the Anvil test asserts both. No public-mempool fallback.
Nested pin lib/stable-yield-accumulator @6eab35c equals the top-level sibling HEAD 6eab35c, so the cross-repo claims above read the same code.
